This role combines hands-on engineering with enterprise AI architecture, responsible AI governance, and executive-level technical advisory. The engineer will work alongside client and delivery teams to design human-agent operating models, agentic workflows, context pipelines, and regulated AI decisioning solutions. Success will be measured by sustainable customer outcomes, production adoption, and the capability transferred to client teams.

ABOUT THE ROLE

At Pika, we're looking for a creative, hands-on AI researcher who can turn the latest models, APIs, and emerging ideas into compelling experiences people want to try and share. You'll combine models across image, video, audio, and language to build workflows, demos, and features that bring people to Pika and contribute to revenue growth.

This is a goal-driven applied research role, open to both full-time hires and interns. You'll take ideas from an initial opportunity through experimentation, implementation, and delivery, then use feedback and results to decide what to improve next. Strong creative judgment, resourcefulness, and fast execution are central to the role.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Find promising opportunities. Stay close to new models, tools, creative formats, and cultural trends. Identify ideas with a clear audience, use case, and potential to drive interest, website traffic, or revenue.

- Build end to end. Combine existing models, APIs, and tools into working multimodal workflows. Own the path from a rough concept to a usable demo, creative asset, or product experience.

- Choose the right amount of research. Test practical approaches quickly. Use lightweight LoRA fine-tuning or targeted post-training when it meaningfully improves the result and fits the project's time budget.

- Deliver frequently. Work in short iteration cycles, set a clear scope for each experiment, and get strong first versions out quickly. Make thoughtful trade-offs between additional research, output quality, cost, and time to delivery.

- Create work ready to share. Produce compelling demos and creative outputs that the team can use for social media, launches, and other growth efforts. Personally posting on or managing social channels is not required.

- Learn from results. Use audience response, product feedback, and relevant traffic or revenue signals to decide which ideas to refine, expand, or stop.

- Make successful work reusable. Leave working workflows, examples, and concise documentation so the team can reproduce and build on what you deliver.

- Hands-on experience building with generative AI models, APIs, or creative workflows, with examples of work you have taken from idea to a working result.

- Strong prototyping and coding skills: you can connect tools, debug a pipeline, and make an end-to-end experience work.

- A creative, entrepreneurial mindset and good judgment about what makes an output compelling, useful, and worth sharing. You enjoy the pace and resourcefulness of a hackathon: testing ideas quickly and getting a working result into people's hands.

- Curiosity across modalities and the ability to learn unfamiliar models and tools quickly.

- Ownership and comfort with tight timelines: you can prioritize, simplify an approach, and recognize when shipping and learning is more valuable than further polishing.

- A clear connection between technical choices and the intended user or business outcome.

HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

- Experience as a startup founder or early-stage startup team member, or actively building and testing startup ideas.

- Hackathon wins or standout hackathon projects that demonstrate rapid prototyping, resourcefulness, and end-to-end execution.

- LoRA fine-tuning, lightweight model adaptation, or other targeted post-training.

- Combining image, video, audio, or language models in a single workflow.

- Building creative demos, interactive prototypes, or AI experiences that reached real users.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

You deliver a steady stream of compelling, usable experiments; turn the strongest ideas into repeatable workflows; and use each release to learn what attracts users and contributes to Pika's growth. Success depends on the quality, speed, and impact of what you deliver.

Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness the transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide. The Opportunity Within AI for Drug Discovery, our team builds platforms that bring AI agents, machine learning models, scientific tools, and data into the hands of drug discovery scientists. You have migrated a production system to a new framework or backend while minimizing downtime. You have scaled a service horizontally and have navigated failure modes around in-memory state, sticky sessions, background workers, DB connections. You understand the practical requirements of production AI-enabled applications, including observability, evaluation, deployment, reliability, and iteration. You can translate ambiguous product or scientific requirements into pragmatic technical architectures and implementation plans. You have led delivery of complex workstreams and can coach other engineers. For the Principal AI Engineer level: Typically BS + 7-12 years, MS + 5-10 years, or PhD + 2-7 years of relevant experience. A track record of owning architecture and outcomes for a complex, multi-team platform, and of being the person others go to for technical decisions. You have strong working knowledge of LLMs and agentic frameworks, including evaluation and model validation practices, and the guardrails needed to run autonomous agents safely. Influence beyond your own team: shaping shared standards, guiding architectural decisions, and mentoring senior engineers. Preferred Qualifications Experience building AI- or ML-enabled applications, agentic systems, or platforms that integrate models, tools, and data. Experience with agent orchestration, tool calling, state management, human-in-the-loop workflows, retrieval, tracing, and Model Context Protocol. Experience with model serving, scientific computing workloads, workflow engines, event-driven architectures, queues, or distributed job-execution systems. Experience designing data platforms that combine raw data, derived features, model outputs, metadata, provenance, and large computational artifacts. Experience with cloud infrastructure, containers, Kubernetes, Helm, load testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and production observability. Experience in computational biology, bioinformatics, cheminformatics, computational chemistry, protein engineering, drug discovery, or another scientific computing domain. Experience running untrusted or model-generated code safely (sandboxing, container isolation, least-privilege service accounts). Deep experience with multi-agent orchestration, including evaluation frameworks and guardrails. # AI Engineer — AI-Native Product Engineering

**Location: Mountain View, CA**

## About the Team

We are rethinking how software is built in an AI-native world.

AI is becoming the default way we design, build, test, debug, and operate software. Engineers on this team work with coding agents to ship production products quickly, while setting the architecture, context, quality standards, and guardrails that make AI-generated software reliable.

This role is **frontend-leaning, but not frontend-limited**. We are moving away from traditional frontend/backend boundaries. You will start from strong client-side product engineering skills and use AI to work effectively across APIs, backend services, data flows, and developer tooling.

The expectation is simple: **own the problem end to end, not just one layer of the stack.**

## What You’ll Do

* **Build user-facing products end to end.** Own features from product requirements and frontend architecture through API integration, backend changes, testing, rollout, and production metrics.
* **Use AI as a core development tool.** Work with coding agents to generate, refactor, test, debug, and understand code, while providing the context and validation needed for production quality.
* **Own frontend architecture and product quality.** Build maintainable component systems, state and data flows, performance-sensitive experiences, and reliable testing patterns for consumer-scale products.
* **Cross frontend/backend boundaries.** Make the API or backend changes needed to complete a product experience rather than handing work off at team boundaries.
* **Set a high bar for AI-generated code.** Review outputs critically and use automated tests, observability, staged rollout, and rollback mechanisms to verify correctness.
* **Improve the AI-native engineering workflow.** Turn repetitive development work into reusable agent workflows, tooling, conventions, and playbooks that make the team faster.
* **Modernize existing systems.** Refactor legacy frontend and service code incrementally so both engineers and AI agents can understand and modify it safely.
* **Own production outcomes.** Investigate performance issues, regressions, and incidents using logs, metrics, experiments, and AI-assisted debugging.

## What We’re Looking For

* **3+ years of software engineering experience**, with strong depth in frontend or client-side product engineering.
* Strong JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals and hands-on experience with React or a comparable modern frontend framework.
* Experience shipping meaningful user-facing features in production and making frontend architecture decisions around components, state, data flow, performance, or testing.
* Evidence that you can work beyond the frontend layer — for example, designing or modifying APIs, backend services, data contracts, or developer tooling.
* Hands-on use of modern AI coding tools or coding agents as part of real development work, not only occasional autocomplete.
* Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to reason about system behavior, debugging, reliability, testing, and performance.
* Ability to learn unfamiliar technologies quickly and use AI effectively to expand into adjacent parts of the stack.
* Strong product mindset: you care about user experience and business outcomes, not just implementation.
* Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where engineers help define the solution rather than simply execute a detailed specification.

## Bonus Points

* Experience building AI-native or agent-powered user experiences.
* Experience building or operating coding agents, LLM workflows, or developer productivity tools.
* Backend experience with Java, Kotlin, Python, Node.js, or similar technologies.
* Experience with recommendation, feed, search, ads, growth, or other large-scale consumer products.
* Experience improving web performance, experimentation infrastructure, design systems, or CI/CD quality gates.
* Experience shipping 0→1 products in a small, highly autonomous team.

About the Team
Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we’re setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

**About Niantic Spatial**

We are building for the >80% of economic activity that happens beyond the reach of screens. AI has learned from the text, images and video online, but it still lacks an accurate understanding of physical space.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

**About the Team**

Localization is where the map meets the moment. Our localization team builds the living geospatial world model and the centimeter-level Visual Positioning System (VPS) that lets people and robots know exactly where they are, from any camera, almost anywhere on Earth.

That system is learned, not hand-built. Our localization stack has moved from classical geometry to visual models trained on billions of posed images — models that have to be accurate to the centimeter, robust to lighting and seasons and clutter, and fast enough to run in production for every query. This team sits at the junction of research and production: we take what works in a paper, make it work on our data, and make it work for customers.

**About the Role**

We're hiring an AI Engineer, Computer Vision, to contribute to the deep learning models at the heart of our localization system. Working alongside experienced researchers and engineers, you'll help train and iterate on the visual models — feature extractors, matchers, pose regressors, and retrieval models — that turn a single image into a precise position in the world.

This is a full-loop environment. You'll get exposure to the entire pipeline: the data the model learns on, training, evaluation, and the service that runs it in production. You'll be surrounded by people who care deeply about correctness — where a loss curve going down is not the same as a system getting better — and you'll grow into that rigor quickly.

**What You'll Do**

* **Train and Evaluate Models —** Implement, train, and evaluate visual localization models in PyTorch: local feature extraction and matching, image retrieval, pose regression, and scene-coordinate regression. Iterate on architectures, loss functions, and training loops to improve accuracy on real production captures.
    
* **Build Data Pipelines —** Contribute to high-throughput ingestion and preprocessing pipelines that turn raw imagery, poses, and 3D point clouds into training-ready datasets, including curation, sampling, and augmentation.
    
* **Run Experiments at Scale —** Run training jobs across GPU environments on our 30-billion-image corpus, working with senior engineers and ML Infrastructure to keep experiments reproducible and results interpretable.
    
* **Extend the Benchmark —** Help build and maintain the evaluation suite for localization — pose accuracy, recall across lighting and season changes, and latency under production load — so results are comparable across model versions.
    
* **Support Production Deployment —** Work with senior engineers to take models from checkpoint toward serving: export, inference optimization, and monitoring once live. Learn what it means to own a model end-to-end, not just hand off a checkpoint.
    
* **Bridge Research and Product —** Work with the Research team and Real-World Test Lab to understand how field failures translate into training data and benchmark improvements.
    

**What You'll Bring**

* Experience training deep learning models for computer vision tasks in PyTorch — through coursework, research, internships, or early industry work.
    
* Foundational understanding of at least one of: visual localization, learned feature matching, image retrieval, pose estimation, SLAM, or structure-from-motion, and the 3D geometry underneath them (camera models, epipolar geometry, pose parameterizations).
    
* Comfort working with large image or 3D datasets — preprocessing, curation, and understanding how data quality affects model behavior.
    
* Familiarity with GPU-based training and the ability to read and reason about training runs — identifying whether a bottleneck is in data loading, compute, or model architecture.
    
* Strong Python skills and a habit of writing code that others can rerun and build on.
    
* A bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, computer vision, robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
    

**Nice to Have**

* Published or contributed to work on learned localization, visual place recognition, scene-coordinate regression, or vision foundation models (CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, NeurIPS, 3DV, or equivalent).
    
* Experience with large-scale self-supervised or multi-view pretraining, or fine-tuning vision foundation models for geometric tasks.
    
* Exposure to inference optimization for edge or mobile hardware (TensorRT, ONNX, CoreML, or similar).
    
* Experience with petabyte-scale spatial data: point clouds, meshes, posed image collections, or geospatial indexing.
    
* Background in robotics, augmented reality, 3D reconstruction, digital twins, or autonomous systems.
    
* Prior industry or research internship experience shipping or contributing to a production CV system.
